thread:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's rollout (rollout-6b3) we started seeing intermittent 20–70ms tail spikes on the serving path that correlate with KV pager activity. Noticed on a few Dedicated nodes.

bot-kv-alert: [ALERT] kv-pager-events increased 8x in last 30m on eu-west-1-prod-gpupool (pager_evictions=2864, reuse_hits_down=0.6).

ajay: I rolled the LRU heuristic tweak in to favor recency scoring + eviction momentum. Did we change any normalization for long contexts?

maria: yeah ajay, we introduced 'momentum' that decays older entries faster. It was intended to help cold-start churn, but the rollout flagged ~30% of nodes.

tess: grabbing profiles. can you post the kv stats endpoint?

maria: curl http://internal-metrics/kv/stats | jq '. | {pager_evictions, fifo_evictions, lru_evictions, reuse_score_mean, avg_context_len}'

```
{"pager_evictions":2864,"fifo_evictions":1220,"lru_evictions":1644,"reuse_score_mean":0.12,"avg_context_len":5140}
```

liam: avg_context_len 5k -> we cross the long-context boundary. previous tests were <2k. momentum + small reuse scores might be evicting entries still needed for long continuations.

olga: profiler top samples (kv pager):
```
# time   samples   symbol
0.42s   140       kv::lookup_cached
0.35s   110       kv::pager::evict_batch
0.12s    30       runtime::serve_token
```

ajay: interesting — pager::evict_batch CPU spikes line up with a large batching burst; batching changed too (heuristic switched to prefer lower-latency microbatches). Could be interacting.

tess: hypothesis: momentum normalization scales poorly with reuse_score for entries with very large KV value sizes => undercounts reuse and triggers eviction; combined with changed batching we push many requests that reference long contexts and force reloads.

maria: can we repro with synthetic replay? bench-kv has a long-context profile.

liam: running: `bench-kv --profile=long-context --concurrency=64 --duration=5m` now.

bot-kv-alert: [INFO] synthetic run started on test-node-12. collecting pager traces at /tmp/pager-traces.tar.gz

olga: while that's running, suggestion: toggle rollout to previous heuristic on a couple nodes: `/ops/rollout revert rollout-6b3 --targets=node-23,node-29` — reduces blast radius.

ajay: done revert on node-23. monitoring.

maria: node-23 tail latencies dropped to baseline within ~45s after revert. node-29 still in progress.

liam: bench run produced reproducible pager bursts. grabbing counters:
```
pager_evictions=980, reuse_misses=1340, disk_reads=980, avg_kv_size=12.4KB
```

ajay: confirmed. repro steps look solid. I think root cause: a bug in the momentum normalization where we divide by (context_len + 1) instead of max(context_len, 1) in float path leading to underflow for context_len > 4096 due to an optimization that kept values in float16 temporarily. Basically reuse_score became ~0 for many entries.

olga: nice catch. that explains correctness/regression. fix plan: 1) rollback rollout cluster-wide, 2) patch normalization (avoid float16 path), 3) add unit+stress tests for long contexts + hammering batching, 4) add alert that ties pager_evictions to reuse_score_mean drops.

maria: updated the incident runbook with those steps. I'll start the patch PR now. @ajay can you coordinate the rollback complete and the private PR?

ajay: on it. PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/kv/compare/fix/momentum-norm (WIP).

tess: adding a small microbenchmark to ci that reproduces the bench-kv scenario so we catch future regressions.

maria: postmortem notes for later: interaction between batching heuristic + eviction normalization is a classic cross-layer perf regression. We should add a perf-test matrix that includes combinations (batching variant x eviction policy x avg_context_len).

liam: also adding a metric: kv_reuse_score_p90 and kv_pager_evictions_rate to the perf dashboard.

bot-kv-alert: [RESOLVED] paging burst subsided on nodes with revert. monitoring continues.

maria: thanks everyone. follow-up: PR + tests + dashboard by EOD tomorrow. will assign owners in the runbook. :thumbsup:
